one_line: A WebMCP creative canvas for agents and humans to compose structured visual designs together.
what_it_does: Provides structured objects, spatial context, and design operations for agent-assisted canvas composition.
leverage_rationale: Structured scene and spatial operations should materially reduce coordinate-level UI friction, but the packet has no runtime or video evidence.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and description specify structured design tools, object geometry, and spatial relationships.
No frame sheets or transcript; only a Devpost packaging screenshot is supplied.
execution_rationale: The concept is coherent, but execution is only claimed in prose and cannot be checked end-to-end from the supplied evidence.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive.
No video frames, transcript, or runtime capture; gallery_images=0.
impact_rationale: Creative practitioners and agent-assisted design workflows have a clear problem around layout reliability, and the proposed structured canvas addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Description identifies collisions, hierarchy, and spatial reasoning as the target problem.
Canvas supports text, images, shapes, frames, and layouts.
creativity_rationale: Treating the canvas as spatially legible shared state is a fresh interaction model for agent-assisted visual design.
creativity_evidence: Concept centers on agents understanding space rather than clicking arbitrary pixels.
Human-agent co-design is central to the stated product.
usability_note: Potentially approachable, but no usable interface evidence is provided.
red_flags: Very thin evidence packet; visual execution claims cannot be checked.
standouts: Spatially structured canvas abstraction for agents.
advance_reason: Coherent and promising, but insufficient evidence for a confident Stage 1 advance.

one_line: A planning workspace that analyzes changed constraints and prepares human-reviewable plan adaptations.
what_it_does: Simulates a launch-budget reduction, identifies affected tasks and conflicts, and produces an approval proposal.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured plan state and proposal generation are useful beyond generic UI driving, though the same outcome remains possible with agent automation at real friction.
leverage_evidence: Story describes constraint analysis over tasks, conflicts, alternatives, and budget adjustments.
Screenshot visibly includes Simulate Constraint Change, Review Proposal, Agent Activity, and WebMCP Tools.
execution_rationale: The dashboard and described workflow are coherent, but the paused Devpost media does not prove the central change-to-approved-proposal flow executes.
execution_evidence: Screenshot shows a consistent Product Launch dashboard with budget values and proposal review UI.
No submitted frame sheets or transcript; demo media is paused.
impact_rationale: Project and operations teams have a concrete recurring problem in adapting plans when constraints change; the proposed workflow has credible value.
impact_evidence: Specific budget-change scenario from $50,000 to $40,000 is described.
Human approval is retained for consequential plan changes.
creativity_rationale: Constraint-reactive planning with an agent preparing actionable change proposals is a fresh synthesis beyond generic planning chat.
creativity_evidence: Concept focuses on impact analysis and adaptation rather than merely displaying a plan.
Agent activity and proposal review are integrated into the workspace.
usability_note: Visible dashboard is legible and workflow-oriented, though live interaction is unverified.
red_flags: Central workflow is presented through a paused media thumbnail rather than observable execution.
advance_reason: Strong problem-solution fit and coherent visible packaging justify advancing despite limited execution evidence.

one_line: A supplier portal exposing governed WebMCP tools for agent-assisted B2B invoice and payment workflows.
what_it_does: Lets agents submit invoices, resolve exceptions, provide evidence, open cases, and track payments with human review gates.
leverage_rationale: Structured governed operations across supplier-portal workflows replace brittle portal clicking and costly bespoke integrations; the agent is central.
leverage_evidence: Story claims 12 governed WebMCP tools covering submission, exceptions, evidence, cases, and payment tracking.
Screenshot shows invoice exception queues, supplier cases, agent panel, and Submit batch controls.
execution_rationale: Authenticated portal scope, coherent UI, and demo media indicate a substantial implementation, but available visual evidence is packaging-level and not end-to-end proof.
execution_evidence: Demo marked alive; public repository exists.
Screenshot shows a consistent supplier finance portal and agent workflow surface.
No transcript and frame-sheet analysis was rate-limited.
impact_rationale: Finance teams and suppliers face real repetitive portal work and integration costs; direct agent access with approval is a credible high-value solution.
impact_evidence: Story identifies repetitive supplier payment work and fragile portal integrations.
Concrete invoice, exception, case, and payment workflows are named.
creativity_rationale: The concept is an ambitious and practical application of agent-native supplier operations, with human-in-the-loop controls.
creativity_evidence: Uses the supplier portal itself as the agent surface rather than a separate dashboard.
Governed multi-operation workflow is more than a single automation.
usability_note: Portal surfaces appear domain-specific and organized; authentication and finance complexity may raise onboarding cost.
red_flags: Video execution details could not be independently checked in this pass.
standouts: Strong practical WebMCP leverage and human approval framing for B2B finance.
advance_reason: High leverage and impact with credible implementation evidence; advance.

one_line: An evidence-bound, single-use approval lease that lets native WebMCP execute exactly one refund.
what_it_does: Binds a human approval to order and invoice evidence, validates it at execution, rejects replay, and records durable audit state.
leverage_rationale: The native WebMCP action is constrained by live evidence, identity, expiry, and exactly-once semantics in a way general UI driving cannot replicate comparably well.
leverage_evidence: Story specifies 120-second, one-execution leases bound to order and invoice.
Claims exactly one refund, durable Firestore ledger, paired native tools, and denied replay.
Screenshot visibly presents WebMCP and charge/refund approval framing.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete consequential-action workflow with explicit crash and replay tests; no frame sheets were independently inspectable due rate limit, so confidence is bounded.
execution_evidence: Detailed claimed sequence covers purchase, invoice parsing, approval, lease, execution, and replay denial.
Public repo, live demo, 10 gallery images, and three submitted frame sheets listed.
impact_rationale: Preventing duplicate or unauthorized financial actions is a real high-stakes problem, and the evidence-bound approval design directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Concrete duplicate $18 charge scenario and refund balance are described.
Human approval and replay rejection are explicit safety outcomes.
creativity_rationale: Evidence leases combine approval semantics, native WebMCP pairing, and exactly-once execution into a memorable interaction and safety model.
creativity_evidence: Single-use approval ticket metaphor is pursued through expiry, binding, and replay denial.
Chrome relay is deliberately constrained to one paired shop tab.
usability_note: Strong safety affordances, though pairing and evidence concepts add complexity.
red_flags: Claims are unusually detailed but visual execution could not be fully inspected due transient vision rate limiting.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and strong high-stakes use case justify advancing.

one_line: A private browser-local structured research editor that exposes research to agents through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Organizes links, notes, people, posts, videos, and sources into typed outlines agents can inspect and suggest edits to.
leverage_rationale: Browser-local structured research with no login, plugin, or server gives an agent reliable shared state and portable access beyond UI scraping.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly states no login/server/plugin and WebMCP connection to ChatGPT.
Screenshot preview shows structured research hierarchy and source ledger with URLs.
execution_rationale: The product concept and visible research UI are coherent, with public repo and live demo, though the paused packaging media does not prove agent editing end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Public repository and four gallery images are listed.
Screenshot shows a research page, typed hierarchy, and cited sources.
No transcript; frame sheets not independently inspected due rate limit.
impact_rationale: Researchers and knowledge workers have a clear need for private, structured, revisable research that agents can help improve.
impact_evidence: Typed sources and connections support research organization and provenance.
Human reviews agent suggestions before applying changes.
creativity_rationale: A portable browser-local research kernel plus agent collaboration without accounts or plugins is a notably original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Private in-browser data model and WebAssembly reader are part of the stated architecture.
Research is exposed as structured semantic objects rather than plain text.
usability_note: Low setup burden is attractive; the research type system may require learning.
red_flags: Agent invocation and applied-edit result are not proven by the static screenshot.
standouts: No-login, browser-private research state connected directly to agents.
advance_reason: Strong agent-state leverage, credible research value, and distinctive architecture.

one_line: A library that turns mutating WebMCP calls into human-released proposals priced against live routing.
what_it_does: Holds risky actions, shows before/after and current execution cost, supports release/change/refuse, and can abort write tools.
leverage_rationale: The site supplies action semantics and live routing data unavailable to generic browser confirmation, making agent-human collaboration materially safer and more precise.
leverage_evidence: Story contrasts site-aware pricing with generic browser confirmation.
Two demos show live Jupiter routing and a team access console.
Screenshot shows a 90-billion-BONK proposal with Release, Change, and Refuse controls.
execution_rationale: A library plus two domain demos and concrete risk calculations indicate strong scope coherence, though the video itself is not fully verified here.
execution_evidence: Public repo, live demo, four gallery images, and three frame sheets are listed.
Claimed routing output quantifies $93,842 return on a $268,000 position versus 0.08% on deeper liquidity.
Visible proposal UI is coherent.
impact_rationale: Agent-mediated financial and administrative writes need contextual approval; live cost/risk visibility provides credible value for operators.
impact_evidence: Concrete price-impact problem is described.
Human can refuse with a reason and later agent reads that reason back.
creativity_rationale: The proposal-as-priced-action model is a memorable interaction pattern that extends approval beyond yes/no into site-specific consequence inspection.
creativity_evidence: Same library spans crypto portfolio and non-financial team access demos.
Abort-signal tool removal and reason-preserving refusal deepen the concept.
usability_note: Clear release/change/refuse affordances; financial terminology and large numbers raise risk of misuse.
red_flags: Live routing and transaction claims are primarily textual in the available packet.
standouts: Contextual, site-owned pricing before human release of agent writes.
advance_reason: Distinctive and high-leverage safety primitive with multiple demos.

impact_evidence: Specific CPU, motherboard, GPU, PSU, budget, aesthetics, and FPS concerns are addressed.

creativity_rationale: Agent-native co-shopping with a shared build is a fresh synthesis of storefront and configuration assistant patterns.
creativity_evidence: Recommendations appear directly in the storefront with goal impact and trade-offs.

usability_note: The component-oriented storefront and explicit build states appear approachable.
red_flags: Compatibility correctness and agent execution are not independently demonstrated.
standouts: Good human-agent shared-state shopping model for a complex purchase.
No taxonomy-perfect secondary category; commerce is primary.

impact_evidence: Targets arranging biological illustrations, labels, connectors, and layouts.

one_line: An agent-ready accounting workspace for inspecting feeds, matching invoices, staging reconciliations, and human-approved payments.
what_it_does: Exposes structured tools for accounts, transactions, invoice search, reconciliation suggestions, exceptions, and payment drafts.
leverage_rationale: Structured financial retrieval and staged reconciliation are materially safer and more precise than an agent clicking a complex accounting dashboard.
leverage_evidence: Story lists seven finance tools including account/transaction inspection, invoice search, matching, and staged actions.

impact_evidence: Specific bank-feed, invoice-match, exception, reconciliation, and payment-draft workflows.

Separates investigation/preparation from consequential approval.

one_line: A scheduling control room where agents propose repairs to live events while organizers and speakers retain approval authority.
what_it_does: Reads schedules and constraints, proposes repairs, collects affected-speaker confirmations, revalidates, applies, and supports undo.
leverage_rationale: Stable domain operations, shared saved state, hard-constraint validation, and proposal invalidation make agent collaboration substantially more reliable than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Story explicitly contrasts shared WebMCP state with disconnected chat and generic clicking.
Claims 10 native tools, stable IDs, constraint preservation, revalidation, and invalidation of stale proposals.
Screenshot packaging describes affected-speaker confirmation gate and blocked state.
execution_rationale: The workflow covers disruption through approval, rejection, next-best plan, validation, and undo, with strong coherence; direct observation remains limited.
execution_evidence: Public repo, live demo, five gallery images, and three frame sheets listed.
Packet describes two-session repair, honest blocked state, weekly timetable reset, and confirmation gate.
impact_rationale: Event organizers face real-time coordination failures with costly human consequences; constraint-aware repairs and confirmations directly address the problem.
impact_evidence: Specific delayed-speaker, unavailable-room, capacity, timing, and turnover constraints.
Organizer and affected speakers remain in the approval loop.
creativity_rationale: Treating schedule repair as a shared, revalidated negotiation with affected-person confirmations is an original and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Decline/rejection triggers a distinct next-best plan.
New edits invalidate stale proposals while undo preserves the original disruption.
usability_note: Control-room framing and explicit blocked states support trust; scheduling domain complexity remains.
red_flags: Frame-sheet contents were not fully inspectable because vision requests hit a transient rate limit.
standouts: Deep constraint handling and multi-party approval in a live scheduling workflow.
advance_reason: Excellent fit between WebMCP shared state and a real coordination problem; advance.
